headline: AWS reaccelerates; profit jump is mostly a one-time gain
summary_short: Amazon's Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 19.6% y/y to $200.6B and operating income grew 43.2% y/y to $27.5B on AWS's fastest growth in 18 quarters (+37% y/y to $42.2B), while diluted EPS jumped to $5.75 as net income was lifted by a $53.4B non-operating gain tied to the Anthropic investment.
summary_long: Net sales rose 19.6% y/y to $200.6B (+10.5% q/q), led by AWS's 37% y/y growth to $42.2B — its fastest pace in 18 quarters — plus 16% North America and 15% International growth. Operating income climbed 43.2% y/y to $27.5B, driven mainly by AWS leverage (income +64% y/y to $16.6B, margin 39.4%). Net income of $62.6B and diluted EPS of $5.75 were dominated by $53.4B of non-operating pre-tax income, primarily from the Anthropic investment, not core operations. TTM free cash flow swung to a $7.6B outflow from an $18.2B inflow on a $66.1B y/y capex rise for AI infrastructure. Amazon guided Q3 2026 net sales to $197.0B-$202.0B and operating income to $22.5B-$26.5B. Stockholders' equity rose to $551.6B; cash was $78.2B.

Also: the shard's long_term_debt_usd_m KPI (132,995) does not reconcile with this release's face balance-sheet 'Long-term debt' line (128,894) — likely a different XBRL tag scope (debt-schedule footnote total vs. the net balance-sheet line) — so long-term debt was left out of the composed KPI list rather than propagating the unreconciled figure. Free cash flow is disclosed by Amazon only on a trailing-twelve-month basis, not quarterly, so the FCF KPI/delta above are both TTM figures, per the release's own supplemental table.
